title: Multiplication Table (Practicing Multiplication by One-Digit Numbers)

text.text:
#### Practicing Multiplication by One-Digit Numbers

There are three levels: a one-digit number multiplied by another one-digit number; a two-digit number by a one-digit number; and a three-digit number by a one-digit number. The multiplication is written vertically and solved column by column, starting from the units.

- The light blue squares are the ones carried from the previous order.
- Use the up button to repeat the column's group of squares and the down button to remove one repetition, until the group is repeated as many times as the one-digit number.
- Each complete group of ten squares becomes the carry to the next order; the squares left outside the last group of ten are the digit that stays in the column.

**Example: 3 × 4.** The column repeats the group of 3 squares four times: 3 × 4 = 12. One group of ten is formed, which is the 1 carried, and 2 squares stay outside — that is the digit 2.

When you finish, you receive a medal and move on to the next problem.

#### The Game

Repeat the group of squares until it appears as many times as the one-digit number, then go to the next column.
